structured_output.strongest_bear_case: This is a ticker-hijack of Tesla, one of a serial run of more than 10 identical "TSLA/Tesla" launches in the past ~26 hours. It is not a narrative the token owns. It lists @Tesla and tesla.com as its links with no connection to Tesla, has no DexScreener profile and no description. Every earlier TSLA copy in the packet now shows $0 liquidity. One launched ~3h earlier did ~$1M in hourly volume before dying, which fits a launch, pump and abandon cycle that repeats on the same ticker. The flow looks like distribution, not organic demand. There are 2,280 unique buyers but only 104 unique sellers, and those 104 made ~2,000 sells (~19 each), consistent with a small set of wallets feeding tokens into retail buying. The packet's wallet-graph scan flagged 112 connected insider wallets, including a 74-wallet group that received tokens by transfer. GMGN tags 53 bundler and 60 rat-trader (insider) wallets. Top-10 holders hold 96% on GeckoTerminal's count, which may include the pool. The token was created and migrated in the same second on the Meteora virtual curve (no organic bonding phase), and its logo image is a duplicate of 3 others. My search found no positive Tesla or Musk catalyst for a 00:00 UTC pump. Recent news is negative: a federal safety investigation into the Cybercab, and the stock dropped after the Sept 4 Cybercab update.

The seller count widening and the price holding for hours after the other copies die. Confirmation that the LP is actually burned or locked, and that the 74-wallet transfer group is not selling.

The two LP-lock readings conflict and I did not resolve them. The two top-10 concentration figures also conflict (GeckoTerminal 96% vs GMGN 1.95%), probably because one counts pool/vault accounts. The bear case rests mainly on packet on-chain data plus the pattern of copies.
